# Review - PR 507 @ 6122bb19dc263447bd32cdd588c608772ccdda32

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: 0a2182d59af621ebbd6a36b03c79c77c48566d53. Workflow-tooling change of 1390 insertions over 10 files (new `pr_train.py`, an integration mode in `ci.sh`, member leases in `checked-push.sh`, one optional keyword on `pr_merge.run_gate`, protocol/EVOLUTION prose and 529 lines of fixtures); no Lean sources are touched, so the faithfulness and proof-integrity checks apply vacuously.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (prose; changes) results/telemetry/events.md:7736 - the branch adds a second, empty `## 2026-09-12 - PR532 CI inherited an orphaned escalation reason` heading directly above `## 2026-09-12 - Proof-packet CI inherits an escalation reason`; the real section with that title is still at line 7768 and `github/main` carries it exactly once. The duplicate has no bullets and is a merge artifact introduced at 26ecf158, so publishing this train would put a bogus empty section into the canonical append-only incident log, against this branch's own stated rule that both append-only histories "retain their original line order and multiplicities" (events.md entry for `orc-502-20260909-03`). Fix: delete line 7736 and leave the populated section at 7768 untouched.
- [ ] F2 (code; minor) local/bin/pr_train.py:1 (commit 6122bb19 subject) - the head commit subject `fix(local): owner-authorized train publication contract, claims and post-push check` is 83 characters; `AGENTS.md:584` requires the subject under 72, and the reviewer persona makes commit conventions part of the review. A subject cannot be corrected after merge, and the F1 correction needs a new head anyway. Fix: amend to something like `fix(local): narrow the train publication contract` while re-pushing the F1 fix.

## Review

I reviewed the full main-relative change (base `a306f622` = merge-base with `github/main`), read every hunk of all ten changed files, and checked the change against the owner-authorized narrower contract of 2026-09-18 rather than against a server-side member predicate.

Contract part A, claims bracket the window. `run_train` (pr_train.py:597-607) enters `member_claims` inside the `ExitStack` immediately after the train and per-PR file locks and *before* `git fetch`, `primary_at` and the first `members_at` call, so no gate reads a member outside the claim. The claims stay held through `verify_manifest` (which runs as a child process of `checked-push.sh`, itself invoked inside the stack), through the transport, and through `moved_members`; `record()` runs in the inner `finally`, and only then does the stack unwind and release. `member_claims`' own `finally` releases every claim already taken on the refusal path, and `GateFailure` is a `LayerError` subclass (pr_merge.py:144) so both `members_at` and `main()` classify it correctly.

Contract part A, refusal on a held member. `claim_call(..., "claim", "main", "train", N)` maps exit 3 to `GateFailure` naming the holder; `claim.sh` on main treats any open claim of any kind as blocking, and `main-train` matches its `^(main|opus)-[a-z]+$` party-kind pattern, so an Opus fix claim really does stop the train.

Contract parts B and D. `moved_members` (pr_train.py:495-514) re-reads every accepted member ref with one `ls-remote` and compares it with the verified `member["head"]`, treating an absent ref as moved. It sits on the only path after `outcome = "published"` with no early return before it, and any failure inside it propagates, so it cannot be skipped on success. A moved member is excluded from the merge-comment loop by `moved = {row["number"] ...}` / `continue`, is printed, is stored in `publication.json` and in the canonical `events.md` bullet, and finally raises `LayerError`, so the run exits non-zero; GitHub will not show such a PR as merged either, because only its earlier head is an ancestor of main. I ran the six fixtures that exercise exactly these paths in the PR worktree (stubbed Lake, private fixture cache, no machine-wide build lock): refusal on a held member with the earlier claims released, release after success and after a failed build, refusal when a member moves at transport start, post-push detection of a member that moves after the commit with only `issues/1/comments` posted, and the unchanged drop-one-conflict publication - all six pass in 24s.

Contract part C, prose. `issues-prs.md` now states the four parts separately and, in part 2 and part 3, says plainly that a lease is a client-side comparison against the ref advertisement, that an up-to-date member sends no update command so the remote holds no predicate for it, and that the advertisement-to-commit window is an accepted residual reproduced by the 2026-09-17 adjudication. The `checked-push.sh` header and the `verify_manifest` / `moved_members` docstrings say the same thing in the same terms. I found no sentence that still claims an atomic guard over every member, and the EVOLUTION.md entry is dated 2026-09-18 and describes the change accurately.

Other checks. `pr_merge.run_gate`'s new `integration_base` keyword defaults to `None` and the single-PR caller at pr_merge.py:887 does not pass it, so ordinary merge behaviour is byte-for-byte preserved; the three new gate fixtures cover the frozen-base accept, post-freeze movement (telemetry and source) and non-main base. `ci.sh --integration-head` forces `FORCE_ALL`, rejects `--skip-build`/`--only`/a PR argument, re-checks the exact head and cleanliness before and after the run, and - because `--base` is set - takes the `PARTIAL` path, so it posts no statuses and writes the `prtrain-<head>-<head>.partial.json` name that `check_combined_ci` reads; that check requires head, merge base, worktree, `conclusion` and all eight `CI_STEPS` outcomes to be `success`, and the worktree is a fresh `mkdtemp`, so a stale manifest cannot be reused. `checked-push.sh` still refuses `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS` with a manifest, validates each member row's ref format, 40-hex SHA, uniqueness and non-collision with the published ref, requires at least two members, and adds the only `EXIT` trap in the file. Exact-head CI on 6122bb19 is green: `local-ci/summary` plus all eight steps `success`.

Non-blocking notes, no action required for merge. (i) In `moved_members` the recorded `claims` field comes from `claim.sh check <n>` while the train still holds its own claim, so it will always report `main-train <n> claimed ...` and can never name a third-party holder; the evidence is honest but self-referential. (ii) A failed claim release only prints to stderr and does not affect the exit status, and `claim.sh` has no TTL, so a killed train leaves claims that block every other writer until an operator releases them. (iii) The PR description is still the stale Lean proof-packet template listing merge subjects; per the main session's instruction this is metadata the main session corrects, so I do not raise it as a finding.

Not checked: no Lean file is touched, so I ran no `lake env lean` and no build; I did not run the three `real_project` fixtures or the rest of the suite, because they take the machine-wide full-build lock; and I did not exercise a live train against GitHub, which the protocol reserves for the operator after deployment.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=CHANGES_REQUESTED, prose=CHANGES_REQUESTED)
